What I did: - Diagnosed the held usage-2025-04 set: all 24 member pipes (extract-01..extract-24) had blocked writers with detached readers (~4 KB pending each), so start-ready refused to run. - Repaired every pipe with `schedctl pipe reconnect <job> --live`, one call per job (24 total), reattaching each writer to its dedicated reader while the jobs stayed queued. - Verified 0 pipes blocked / 24 connected and no jobs waiting for repair, then started the set with `schedctl start-ready usage-2025-04`. Result: - Set usage-2025-04 is started; all 24 jobs dispatched; the usage-2025-04 analytics dataset is built from the set's current jobs. Why live reconnect instead of `pipe reset --all`: - The whole-set reset requires stopping logstash-forwarder, which would drop the readers' open handles and leave a non-backfillable gap in the off-host log store. Live reconnects touch only the blocked pipes, required no service stoppage on the production host (keeping well clear of the rule against disabling a monitor), and achieved the same end state. Nothing was left undone: the dataset was built successfully.
